scope_note: These are existing cross-subject mathematical suppliers and their exact limits, not a declaration that any planned information-theory proof is already locally supplied. The owner/scaffolder must add each selected item to deps and verify its proof contract. No r5-specific production item is created here.

current_information_theory_item_scan.result: No published information-theory-specific item family was found in items/ during this scan; the information-theory category scaffold is being written by the separate integrator.
current_information_theory_item_scan.consequence: All network-information-theory definitions, operational code models, typicality/coding lemmas, channel/source capacity statements and their local proof chains must be authored in the planned category unless an exact supplier below is adequate.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: finite probability spaces, event probabilities, outcome weights used to model finite alphabets and uniform messages
existing_suppliers.limits: Does not define source/channel codes, entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information, typicality or a coding theorem.
Does not establish independent messages unless independence is separately supplied.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: independence of source messages, independently generated codebooks, and factorized test-channel construction
existing_suppliers.limits: The required independence must follow from the operational model or be an explicit codebook-generation choice; it is not automatic for feedback inputs.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: finite-alphabet mutual independence and its joint-law factorization
existing_suppliers.limits: Does not provide a random-coding or channel-capacity result.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: DMS/DMC sample-product models and i.i.d. source/channel sequences
existing_suppliers.limits: The memoryless factorization must be stated for the particular source or channel; it does not itself prove an AEP or typicality lemma.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: weak-law control of empirical frequencies of finitely many bounded indicator variables in finite-alphabet typicality arguments
existing_suppliers.limits: Not a general AEP for unbounded information density, continuous alphabets, stationary ergodic sources, or arbitrary distortion measures.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: Jensen steps in entropy/KL nonnegativity, rate-distortion convexity and information inequalities when its integrability/convexity premises are met
existing_suppliers.limits: Does not by itself prove entropy chain rules, data processing, typicality, or a coding theorem.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: definitions of finite distribution entropy, finite relative entropy and stochastic matrices
existing_suppliers.limits: Uses natural logarithms and a finite-distribution interface. Convert to bits explicitly. It does not supply conditional entropy/MI chain rules, Markov/data-processing theorems, or coding results. Its quantum-algorithm home does not broaden its theorem scope.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: general measure-theoretic KL divergence and absolute-continuity/support conventions
existing_suppliers.limits: Does not supply information-theoretic chain rules, conditional MI, DPI, or source/channel coding. Uses natural logarithms.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: MI between a finite uniform hypothesis and a general observation, as a KL-to-mixture average
existing_suppliers.limits: Narrower than general `I(X;Y)` or `I(X;Y|Z)` for arbitrary dependent finite random variables. Any extension needs a locally proved definition/equivalence, with units made explicit.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: a finite-uniform-hypothesis Fano/packing lower bound with a reference-law KL term
existing_suppliers.limits: A source-specific specialization is needed to recover the ordinary message-decoding Fano inequality; verify its metric-loss and divergence hypotheses and convert natural-log units. Its name does not mean it proves Shannon's random-coding packing lemma.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: stochastic channel kernels and randomized encoder/decoder interfaces on measurable spaces
existing_suppliers.limits: Does not establish memorylessness, coding capacity, or an output law for a particular model.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: probability laws used by source/channel definitions
existing_suppliers.limits: Finite entropy and information identities still require separate derivations and support checks.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: conditional source/channel law interfaces on its stated measurable spaces
existing_suppliers.limits: Defines a supplied kernel and makes no general existence claim; state standard-Borel or finite-alphabet premises when constructing one.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: factorization steps for independent codebook/source random variables
existing_suppliers.limits: Must not be used after feedback makes current inputs depend on past channel outputs without checking the conditional independence structure.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: finite-dimensional covariance/error-covariance models in Gaussian source/channel proofs
existing_suppliers.limits: Does not justify differential-entropy bounds or Gaussian coding by itself.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: log-determinant Jensen step in the Gaussian two-encoder converse and covariance bounds
existing_suppliers.limits: Requires positive-definite matrices; singular error covariance must be handled separately before applying it.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: convexity premise for time-sharing and rate-distortion/value-function arguments
existing_suppliers.limits: The proof that a proposed rate region is convex or that an auxiliary support bound holds remains local.

existing_suppliers.usable_for: supporting-hyperplane arguments for finite-dimensional convex rate regions
existing_suppliers.limits: Does not give the specific auxiliary-cardinality bound or prove the region characterization.

r5_specific_local_proofs_still_required: Choose and define one finite-alphabet entropy/information convention (bits or nats); define conditional entropy and MI from joint/conditional laws and prove chain rules, nonnegativity, DPI, and the finite Markov implications actually used.

Define DMS, DMC, DM-MAC, DM-BC, DM-IC, DM relay/network, code, independent uniform messages, causal encoders, common/private messages, block error and average/maximal error. State cost and distortion conventions for every theorem.

Define the chosen weak/strong typicality notion and prove the finite-alphabet LLN/AEP, conditional typicality/Markov lemma, joint-typicality packing bounds, covering bounds, typical-average lemma, random-binning collision bounds and simultaneous-decoding error partitions with exact independence conditions.
Prove Slepian–Wolf achievability and converse locally, including the subset-indexed error events and the closure of the polyhedral rate region.

Prove MAC random-coding achievability and Fano/time-coordinate converse; prove convexification and the stated support bound for Q while preserving all needed mutual-information coordinates. Distinguish average from maximal error.
Prove degraded-BC converse after replacing a stochastically degraded channel by its physically degraded equivalent; prove superposition achievability and the specific U cardinality bound.

For the Gaussian two-encoder theorem, prove the continuous-alphabet entropy/covariance inequalities, the CEO coupling and the Gaussian-test-channel equality conditions; document finite-quantization or density arguments for any random-coding achievability step.
For feedback and NNC, define causal probability kernels/directed information before use and prove the chosen block-Markov/compression-index inequalities under their causal product factorizations.
Prove only named exact special cases; keep open general capacity regions as open-problem formulations with current source/status review rather than using bounds as premises.
